recipes.name: Shrimp Gazpacho
ingredients_raw: 64 fluid ounces tomato and clam juice cocktail
3 pounds cooked shrimp, peeled and deveined

steps.text: Combine tomato and clam juice cocktail, shrimp, avocados, tomatoes, cucumbers, onion, cilantro, lemon juice, salt, and pepper together in a large bowl.
Cover the bowl with plastic and refrigerate until ready to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Shrimp Gazpacho
raw_recipe.description: This shrimp gazpacho recipe is so easy and uses unique ingredients like tomato-clam juice cocktail, avocado, and seafood for a refreshing summer soup.

review.reviewBody: This was WONDERFUL! I grew up eating this and it tastes just like my dad used to make. I scaled it down and used what I had on hand. I used a 46 oz of V8 vegetable tomato juice, 1 cucumber, 1 avocado, 1lb of cooked, frozen shrimp that I defrosted under cold water, half of a red onion, half bunch of cilantro, 1/4 lemon juice, salt, pepper and about 1/2 to 1 tsp of cayenne pepper as well as a tsp of worchestire sauce. It turned out so well. Be cautious if you choose to put cayenne in it. As I was making it, it didn't taste very spicy at all so I added a bit more but as it sat in the fridge to chill, the cayenne assumed its full potential and was hot. We love spicy food and it wasn't too spicy for us at all, but wanted to tell others in case they used it and couldn't taste the flavor as they were preparing it.

I cut the recipe down to 4, I used frozen/thawed salad shrimp (otherwise I'd have given them a rough chop), I diced everything very fine & I used cilantro-in-a-tube (about 2 tbps). I also added celery salt, a couple of tbp of EVOO, a tbp of worcestershire (figure it's good in bloody mary's so what the heck), some diced yellow bell pepper & a smidgeon of hubby's hot sauce (it's garlic, serrano peppers, bell peppers & onions, roasted & pureed). I made it up & let it meld in the fridge for a couple of hours & then gave it a squeeze of lime before I served it in chilled bowls. This is a very filling, satisfying gazpacho ...all the accompaniments it needs is some toast & a glass of sauvignon blanc. Thansk for a great recipe Dawn...we really enjoyed it!

I could not use the Clamato Cocktail drink, so I used 24 oz. Organic tomato juice and 16 oz. clam juice. This ratio seemed right to us (I cut the recipe in half and got 6 generous portions) but we really liked the extra juice. I also added 1 TBSP Worcestershire sauce, 2 TBSP Olive Oil and Hot sauce. We also found the recipe needed more salt. I used 2 Lbs. shrimp and chopped them into bit size pieces. (Husband likes the extra protein) We enjoyed this more the next day as the onion flavor mellowed. Over all this was a huge hit. My husband was impressed with how healthy this is and my Father-in-law just enjoyed the flavors. This was a refreshing change of pace. I will make this again. - Huge hit Dawn. Thank you for sharing!

I really liked this. I used 48 ounces of original V-8 and 16 ounces of spicy v-8. Next time I'll cube the cucumbers instead of slicing. If your cooking raw shrimp, steam them and ice them down as soon as they're done. I used a tablespoon of Old Bay seasoning on them while they steamed. This makes a lot of soup, so be prepared to share with neighbors. Because its seafood, consume as soon as possible (I don't that will be a problem).

I pureed half of the veggies and juice, including the avocados. added two cloves of minced garlic and 2 minced jalapenos, in my food processor. Gave it some consistency. Added the rest of the chopped veggie, two tbsp EVOO, one tbsp hot sauce, the 2 remaining cubed avocados and the shrimp. Served ice cold with a nice chardonnay and crusty bread. It was a huge hit at a gourmet dinner. Will make this over and over.

I’ve made this recipe for years, and it’s a family favorite. Pro tip: don’t waste your time dicing everything: put all your ingredients but the shrimp in the food processor and do a rough blend. Don’t liquify it. (You may need to do smaller batches if you have a smaller food processor) Add the shrimp afterward. Do yourself a favor and play with the amount of diced garlic and Tabasco. Awesome light meal for hot summer nights.

I made this last night and let it sit in the fridge to allow the flavors to blend overnight. It was fantastic for lunch today and as I made the whole recipe, will be for many more lunches and dinners! I only made a few slight changes, using Low-Sodium Tomato Juice and a bottle of clam juice to sub for the tomato and clam juice cocktail. I also used 1 SlimCado (Florida Avocado) as it is lower in fat / calories and much bigger than a Hass Avocado. I seeded the cucumbers before cubing and only used 1 pound of salad shrimp. After following the recipe exactly after that...I found it needed a little more seasoning. So, I added about 1 Tbsp low-sodium worcestershire, 1-2 tsp celery salt, and several drops of tobasco. That made it 5 stars! 

With my changes, this came out to 117.9 Calories, 2.5 grams Total Fat (0.2g Saturated, 0.3g Polyunsaturated, 0.1g Monounsaturated), 73.7mg Cholesterol, 208.3mg Sodium, 611.1mg Potassium, 15.5g Total Carbs (2.3g dietary fiber, 6.5g sugar) and 9.9g Protein Per Serving (12 Servings)

Loved it, but it needs some "heat". Such as: Spicy Clamato Juice instead of regular Clamato juice. If one has no red pepper sauce or some other kind of hot sauce (like Tabasco). It adds a bit more flavor. I used some Louisiana hot sauce to taste. Other than that, this recipe is awesome. Mayhaps some cilantro would work as a garnish?

Winner! I've made a lot of gazpacho recipes from this site, and this is by far my fave! I can't wait to make this for family and guests. A wonderful mix of flavors and textures. The use of Clamato is genius and I loved having shrimp in it. Make sure you use Clamato and not V8. I felt like it needed more salt and pepper, but otherwise I wouldn't change a thing! It's quite filling, unlike other gazpachos. I left the peel on the cucumber for added color. I scaled the recipe down, but it was so good I had two servings, and can't wait to have the leftovers for lunch.

Followed this recipe exactly. There are no flavors in this except the taste of clammy tomato juice. Spent an extra 30 mins. adding some flavors, lots of garlic, red wine vinegar, more salt and pepper, tabasco sauce juice of 2 lemons and olive oil. With all that it still pretty tasteless.
I love spicy, so added some fresh serranos from the garden...
Very 👍
This is a delicious, refreshing soup. The directions were easy to follow. It made a large amount. I will definitely be making this again and again.

This is a very easy and delicious recipe! I added some garlic powder because we are garlic nuts and we don't care if we smell like garlic. I also added Worchester sauce because we love it. Subbed celery salt for regular. (a new addition to our foods). Thank you, Dawn! I made this today for tomorrow so the flavors meld. Yum, can't wait!
I like spicy but when I seen 1 TBSP, I chose to start with a tsp! It was awesome (but forgot my tomatoes had Med. Chili peppers
amazing recipe.
My husband, kids and brother in law loved it. I added green, red, yellow and orange peppers and I also added clam juice. Perfect

This is an absolutely wonderful dish! We had friends over and my one friend can’t stand gazpacho. We convinced her to try and she loved it! She asked for this recipe and has made it twice! Bravo Dawn!

Oh my. I do hate to be That Guy who doesn't follow a recipe but reviews it anyway. Here I go, nonetheless. I only had one avocado so I threw in a can of garbanzo beans. I only had one tomato, so I used a can of diced tomatoes. And I added a can of clams because it seemed like a good idea. This turned out well though and I will definitely make it again.
